candidate.answerReason: The attainable slopes form the interval between the two roots of 80t²−280t+199=0. Their sum is 280/80=7/2.

methods.label: Find which slopes meet the ellipse
methods.explanation:
The ratio \(y/x\) is the slope of the line joining the origin to \((x,y)\). Since the ellipse lies in the first quadrant, \(x>0\), so this ratio is defined and positive. Let \(t=y/x\). Substituting \(y=tx\) into the ellipse equation gives
\[
(3t^2+t+2)x^2-(11+20t)x+40=0.
\]
Thus we can find the possible slopes by determining when this quadratic has real roots.

For \(t>0\), its leading coefficient \(A=3t^2+t+2\) is positive. Its discriminant is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta(t)&=(11+20t)^2-160(3t^2+t+2)\\
&=-80t^2+280t-199.
\end{aligned}
\]
Whenever its roots \(u,v\) are real, expanding \(A(x-u)(x-v)\) gives
\[
u+v=\frac{11+20t}{A}>0,
\qquad uv=\frac{40}{A}>0.
\]
Their positive product means they have the same sign, and their positive sum means both are positive. Consequently, \(\Delta(t)\geq0\) is both necessary and sufficient for an allowed intersection.

The downward-opening quadratic \(\Delta(t)\) is negative at \(t=0\), positive at \(t=1\), and negative at \(t=4\). Its nonnegative set is therefore a closed interval with two positive endpoints. These endpoints are the minimum and maximum slopes \(b\) and \(a\); both are attained because a zero discriminant still gives a positive intersection coordinate.

Hence
\[
80t^2-280t+199=80(t-a)(t-b).
\]
Comparing the coefficients of \(t\) gives \(-80(a+b)=-280\), so
\[
\boxed{a+b=\frac72}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
